title: Grateful Dead Live at Temple University on 1970-05-16
lineage: AUD MC > ? > Cass > CD/0 > EAC > WAV > Soundforge > SHN

ai_review.summary: Rough audience‑sourced tape with noisy, muddy mix but captures a brief, high‑energy 1970 Temple Stadium set that shines on New Speedway Boogie.
ai_review.review: The recording is an audience cassette with plenty of crowd chatter and a generally muddy balance—Jerry Garcia’s guitar cuts through, while vocals sit low. Musically the show is short yet lively, remembered for its historic context (the same bill as Jimi Hendrix) and a particularly strong rendition of New Speedway Boogie. Listeners who can overlook the lo‑fi sound find it an enjoyable snapshot of the Dead in 1970.

ai_rating.rationale: Show is praised for its energy and historic value, but recording quality is widely criticized as noisy and muddy; the mixed feedback yields a modest overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Heavy audience noise, low vocal levels, generally muddy mix; however Jerry's guitar is clear. Some reviewers note occasional drop‑outs and an uneven balance typical of a cassette taping.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A short, sub‑hour set that kept high energy throughout; the band delivered joyous, lively playing despite the brief runtime and historic circumstances of sharing the bill with Hendrix.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's guitar comes across very clear on this tape.
